claim: The chromosome passenger complex (CPC) is a complex of four proteins involved in the regulation of key mitotic events: correction of chromosome-microtubule attachment errors, assembly and stability of the spindle assembly checkpoint, and assembly and regulation of the contractile apparatus that drives cytokinesis.
source: The chromosome passenger complex (CPC) is a complex of four proteins involved in the regulation of key mitotic events: correction of chromosome-microtubule attachment errors, assembly and stability of the spindle assembly checkpoint, and assembly and regulation of the contractile apparatus that drives cytokinesis (Carmena et al., 2012; Vader et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research (Carmena et al., 2012; Vader et al., 2006).

claim: The CPC is organized into two modules: a localization module consisting of survivin, borealin, and the N-terminal part of INCENP, and an enzymatic module comprising Aurora B kinase and the C-terminal part of INCENP, called the IN-box.
source: The CPC is organized into two modules. The localization module consists of survivin, borealin, and the N-terminal part of INCENP, whereas the enzymatic module comprises Aurora B kinase and the C-terminal part of INCENP, called the IN-box.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about CPC organization.

claim: The enzymatic activity of Aurora B is essential for the regulatory functions of CPC.
source: The enzymatic activity of Aurora B is essential for the regulatory functions of CPC (Kelly and Funabiki, 2009; Krenn and Musacchio, 2015; Meraldi et al., 2004)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Aurora B has been identified as an attractive target for cancer chemotherapy.
source: so Aurora B has been identified as an attractive target for cancer chemotherapy (Portella et al., 2011), with several inhibitors patented in the last decades (Jing and Chen, 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The activity of the [Aurora B/IN-box] complex increases by at least two orders of magnitude after the complex phosphorylates itself.
source: The activity of the complex increases by at least two orders of magnitude after the complex phosphorylates itself (Zaytsev et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: There are two well-defined autophosphorylation sites in the [Aurora B/IN-box] enzyme complex: a threonine in the Aurora B activation loop and two consecutive serine residues in the TSS motif at the C-terminus of the IN-box.
source: There are two well-defined autophosphorylation sites in the [Aurora B/IN-box] enzyme complex. One is a threonine in the Aurora B activation loop, and the second is located at the C-terminus of the IN-box and consists of two consecutive serine residues in the TSS motif (Bishop and Schumacher, 2002; Honda et al., 2003; Sessa et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The molecular understanding of Aurora B autoactivation was based on a model derived from the structure of the partially phosphorylated enzyme, in which the threonine in the Aurora B activation loop was phosphorylated but the TSS motif of INCENP was either absent or unstructured.
source: Until recently, the molecular understanding of Aurora B autoactivation was based on a model derived from the structure of the partially phosphorylated enzyme, in which the threonine in the Aurora B activation loop was phosphorylated but the TSS motif of INCENP was either absent (Sessa et al., 2005; Sessa and Villa, 2014) or unstructured (Elkins et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: A structural study of the [Aurora C/IN-box] complex provided valuable insight into the conformation the fully phosphorylated enzyme adopts.
source: Recently, a structural study of the [Aurora C/IN-box] complex, which is specific for meiosis but otherwise very similar to the [Aurora B/IN-box] complex, provided valuable insight into the conformation the fully phosphorylated enzyme adopts (Abdul Azeez et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The crystal structure of [Aurora C/IN-box] shows that the activation loop of Aurora C and the IN-box TSS motif interact in the phosphorylated state and stabilize the extended (active) conformation of the activation loop.
source: The crystal structure shows that the activation loop of Aurora C and the IN-box TSS motif interact in the phosphorylated state and stabilize the extended (active) conformation of the activation loop.
evidence: The claim is based on a citation to prior research (Abdul Azeez et al., 2019) mentioned in the preceding sentence.

claim: There is no crystal structure available of the [Aurora B/IN-box] complex in the unphosphorylated state.
source: In addition, there is not crystal structure available of the [Aurora B/IN-box] complex in the unphosphorylated state and therefore, there is an important gap in understanding the conformational changes taking place during the activation process.
evidence: The claim is based on the absence of reported structures in the literature.

claim: An increase in dynamics or local flexibility may facilitate the adoption of the different conformations required during the catalytic cycle.
source: For example, an increase in dynamics or local flexibility may facilitate the adoption of the different conformations required during the catalytic cycle (Boehr et al., 2006; Tzeng and Kalodimos, 2012; Xie et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The transition from a highly dynamic, disordered enzyme to a more structured enzyme has been documented as a form of regulation of enzyme catalysis.
source: On the other hand, the transition from a highly dynamic, disordered enzyme to a more structured enzyme has also been documented as a form of regulation of enzyme catalysis (Wei et al., 2016; Xiao et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The internal dynamics associated with the movements of protein kinase subdomains regulate enzymatic activity.
source: In particular, an intensive line of research on protein kinases has shown that the internal dynamics associated with the movements of the enzyme's subdomains regulate enzymatic activity (Ahuja et al., 2019; Pegram et al., 2021; Taylor and Kornev, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Detailed dynamics analyses are available for several eukaryotic protein kinases activated by phosphorylation, including the closely related Aurora A.
source: While detailed dynamics analyses are available for several eukaryotic protein kinases activated by phosphorylation (Foda et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2019), including the closely related Aurora A (Cyphers et al., 2017; Dodson and Bayliss, 2012; Gilburt et al., 2017; Pitsawong et al., 2018; Ruff et al., 2018; Tomlinson et al., 2022)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The effect of phosphorylation on the dynamic properties of the [Aurora B/IN-box] complex is not yet known.
source: the effect of phosphorylation on the dynamic properties of the [Aurora B/IN-box] complex is not yet known.
evidence: The claim is based on the absence of reported studies in the literature.

claim: In the absence of phosphorylation, there is structural disorder scattered along several regions of the [Aurora B/IN-box] enzyme complex.
source: We found that in the absence of phosphorylation, there is structural disorder scattered along several regions of the enzyme complex.
evidence: The claim is supported by HDX-MS and MD simulation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: In the fully phosphorylated enzyme complex, both Aurora B and the IN-box are structurally organized, resulting in a fully functional enzyme.
source: In contrast, in the fully phosphorylated enzyme complex, both Aurora B and the IN-box are structurally organized, resulting in a fully functional enzyme.
evidence: The claim is supported by HDX-MS and MD simulation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Phosphorylation of each individual site in isolation has only a minor effect on enzymatic activity and structural stability.
source: Phosphorylation of each individual site in isolation has only a minor effect on enzymatic activity and structural stability
evidence: The claim is supported by enzyme kinetics and HDX-MS data on partially phosphorylated intermediates presented in the manuscript.

claim: Simultaneous phosphorylation of the activation loop in Aurora B and the TSS motif in the IN-box synergistically affects the structure and dynamics of the enzyme complex, leading to a dramatic increase in kinase activity.
source: whereas simultaneous phosphorylation of the activation loop in Aurora B and the TSS motif in the IN-box synergistically affects the structure and dynamics of the enzyme complex, leading to a dramatic increase in kinase activity.
evidence: The claim is supported by enzyme kinetics and HDX-MS data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Phosphorylation in the activation loop of Aurora B occurs intramolecularly and prepares the enzyme complex for activation.
source: Further, we identify phosphorylation in the activation loop of Aurora B as a rate-limiting intramolecular event in autoactivation.
evidence: The claim is supported by kinetic experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: Only when both sites are phosphorylated are the global movements of the N- and C-lobes of the enzyme (opening and closing of the active site and twisting between the lobes) coordinated with the movements of the activation loop, resulting in a fully functional kinase.
source: Finally, only when both sites are phosphorylated are the global movements of the N- and C-lobes of the enzyme (opening and closing of the active site and twisting between the lobes) coordinated with the movements of the activation loop, resulting in a fully functional kinase.
evidence: The claim is supported by MD simulation data and PCA analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Comparison of HDX measurements for [Aurora B/IN-box]no-P and [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P reveals several regions of the enzyme complex with profound HDX differences.
source: Comparison of HDX measurements for the two phosphorylation states reveals several regions of the enzyme complex with profound HDX differences (Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by HDX-MS data shown in Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The unphosphorylated form of the enzyme takes up more deuterium in all regions where HDX differences were detected, indicating greater flexibility and lower structural organization.
source: The unphosphorylated form of the enzyme takes up more deuterium in all regions where HDX differences were detected, indicating greater flexibility and lower structural organization.
evidence: The claim is based on HDX-MS data interpretation.

claim: The fully active form, [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P, has a lower HDX, indicating a more rigid structural organization.
source: Consequently, the fully active form, [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P, has a lower HDX, indicating a more rigid structural organization.
evidence: The claim is based on HDX-MS data interpretation.

claim: In Aurora B, there are four regions with high cumulative HDX differences between [Aurora B/IN-box]no-P and [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P.
source: In Aurora B, there are four regions with high cumulative differences (labeled with numbered circles in Figure 1A and in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by HDX-MS data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The first region with high ΔHDX in Aurora B spans residues 120–156 and includes part of the β3-strand, the αB-helix, the catalytic αC-helix, and the loop region following the αC-helix.
source: In Aurora B, the first region with high ΔHDX spans residues 120–156 and includes part of the β3-strand, the αB-helix, the catalytic αC-helix, and the loop region following the αC-helix (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by HDX-MS data shown in Figure 1A-C.

claim: The middle portion of the αC helix is particularly rigid in the phosphorylated enzyme complex and shows >15% HDX protection across all time points.
source: The middle portion of the αC helix is particularly rigid in the phosphorylated enzyme complex (Figure 1C) and shows >15% HDX protection across all time points.
evidence: The claim is supported by HDX-MS data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The αC-helix plays a critical role in the organization of the productive enzyme complex in protein kinases.
source: It is known from studies of other eukaryotic protein kinases that the αC-helix plays a critical role in the organization of the productive enzyme complex (Kornev and Taylor, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The αC-helix contributes to the positioning of the activation segment, which includes the magnesium-binding loop (DFG loop), the activation loop with phosphorylated Aurora BThr248, and the P+1 loop.
source: This helix contributes to the positioning of the activation segment, which includes the magnesium-binding loop (DFG loop), the activation loop with phosphorylated Aurora BThr248, and the P+1 loop (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about protein kinase structure and is illustrated in Figure 1D.

claim: The αC-helix residues contribute to the formation of the R-spine, a series of hydrophobic interactions extending from the N-lobe to the C-lobe of protein kinases, that are critical for the adoption of an active conformation.
source: The αC-helix residues also contribute to the formation of the R-spine, a series of hydrophobic interactions extending from the N-lobe to the C-lobe of protein kinases, that are critical for the adoption of an active conformation (Kornev and Taylor, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Helices αB and αC provide an interacting surface for binding regulators of kinase activity in a variety of protein kinases.
source: In addition, helices αB and αC provide an interacting surface for binding regulators of kinase activity in a variety of protein kinases (Leroux and Biondi, 2020)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Helices αB and αC are a site of interaction between the structurally similar Aurora A kinase and its binding partner TPX2.
source: and are a site of interaction between the structurally similar Aurora A kinase and its binding partner TPX2 (Bayliss et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The second region with high ΔHDX in Aurora B spans residues 205–223 and includes the last five amino acids of the αE-helix, a linker region that includes the major catalytic loop (HRD loop) and the β7-strand.
source: The second region spans residues 205–223 and includes the last five amino acids of the αE-helix, a linker region that includes the major catalytic loop (HRD loop) and the β7-strand.
evidence: The claim is supported by HDX-MS data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The third region with high ΔHDX in Aurora B spans residues 254–272 and includes the end of the activation segment, the αEF-helix, the loop upstream of the αF-helix, and the first turn of the αF-helix.
source: The third region spans residues 254–272 and includes the end of the activation segment, the αEF-helix, the loop upstream of the αF-helix, and the first turn of the αF-helix, which is an important organizer of the C-lobe (Kornev et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by HDX-MS data presented in the manuscript and a citation to prior research.

claim: The fourth region with high ΔHDX in Aurora B spans residues 284–305 and includes the αG-helix and the preceding loop.
source: The fourth region spans residues 284–305 and includes the αG-helix and the preceding loop.
evidence: The claim is supported by HDX-MS data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The αG-helix region is part of the peptide substrate recognition site and is thought to play a regulatory role in protein kinases.
source: This region is part of the peptide substrate recognition site and is thought to play a regulatory role in protein kinases (Ahuja et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The IN-box is highly dynamic with a very fast HDX rate in both [Aurora B/IN-box]no-P and [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P.
source: The IN-box is highly dynamic with a very fast HDX rate in both [Aurora B/IN-box]no-P and [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P (most peptides are fully exchanged at the early time points, Supplementary file 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by HDX-MS data presented in Supplementary file 5.

claim: The only segment of IN-box where differences in deuteration are detected extends from positions 805 to 825 and contains the IN-boxαA helix and the short IN-boxαB helix connected by a linker.
source: The only segment of IN-box where differences in deuteration are detected extends from positions 805 to 825 and contains the only well-defined secondary structure elements: IN-boxαA helix and the short IN-boxαB helix connected by a linker (Figure 1A–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by HDX-MS data shown in Figure 1A-D.

claim: HDX kinetics for the IN-box805-825 region shows a strong component of EX1 kinetics and a smaller component of common EX2 kinetics.
source: HDX kinetics for this region shows a strong component of EX1 kinetics and a smaller component of common EX2 kinetics.
evidence: The claim is supported by HDX-MS data analysis.

claim: EX1 kinetics is indicative of structural unfolding of local protein regions.
source: By definition, EX2 kinetics is common in the native folded state of proteins, while EX1 kinetics are less common in native conditions and is indicative of structural unfolding of local protein regions (Arrington and Robertson, 2000; Chitta et al., 2009; Ferraro et al., 2004; Sperry et al., 2012; Walters et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: In the IN-box805-825 region, two clear isotopic envelopes are observed, a hallmark of EX1 kinetics.
source: In the IN-box805-825 region, we observe the appearance of two clear isotopic envelopes (Figure 1—figure supplement 3), a hallmark of EX1 kinetics.
evidence: The claim is supported by HDX-MS data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The lower mass isotopic peak corresponds to the folded state of IN-box805-825, where the amide-hydrogen bonds are more protected.
source: The lower mass isotopic peak corresponds to the folded state of IN-box805-825, where the amide-hydrogen bonds are more protected.
evidence: The claim is based on interpretation of HDX-MS data.

claim: The high mass isotope peak is indicative of the unfolded state of the IN-box805-825 region, where multiple amide-hydrogen bonds break simultaneously and exchange hydrogen for deuterium.
source: The high mass isotope peak is indicative of the unfolded state of the IN-box805-825 region, where multiple amide-hydrogen bonds break simultaneously and exchange hydrogen for deuterium.
evidence: The claim is based on interpretation of HDX-MS data.

claim: The EX1 behavior was observed in both [Aurora B/IN-box]no-P and [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P, suggesting that IN-box805-825 reversibly switches between the unfolded and folded states regardless of the phosphorylation state.
source: The EX1 behavior was observed in both [Aurora B/IN-box]no-P and [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P, suggesting that IN-box805-825 reversibly switches between the unfolded and folded states regardless of the phosphorylation state.
evidence: The claim is based on interpretation of HDX-MS data.

claim: The higher mass peak appears more rapidly in [Aurora B/IN-box]no-P, suggesting that this region of IN-box visits the unfolded state more frequently in the unphosphorylated form of the enzyme complex.
source: However, the higher mass peak appears more rapidly in [Aurora B/IN-box]no-P, suggesting that this region of IN-box visits the unfolded state more frequently in the unphosphorylated form of the enzyme complex.
evidence: The claim is based on interpretation of HDX-MS data.

claim: Mass photometry measurements at 10 nM enzyme concentration confirm that the interactions between Aurora B and IN-box are stable under the HDX experimental conditions in both phosphorylated and unphosphorylated states.
source: To determine whether the [Aurora B/IN-box] complex remained intact in our HDX experimental conditions, we used mass photometry to measure the molecular weight (MW) of the enzymatic complex, [Aurora B/IN-box]no-P and [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P at low nM concentrations. In both samples, we observed a single uniform peak corresponding to MW of ~44 kD (MWAurora B=35.4 kD; MWIN-box=8 kD), the measurements were performed at 10 nM enzyme concentration. This clearly confirms that the interactions between Aurora B and IN-box are stable under the HDX experimental conditions in the two states, phosphorylated and unphosphorylated, (Figure 1—figure supplement 4)
evidence: The claim is supported by mass photometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: The differences observed by HDX are due to phosphorylation-induced changes in enzyme dynamics rather than dissociation between the two polypeptide chains.
source: and that the differences observed by HDX are due to phosphorylation-induced changes in enzyme dynamics rather than dissociation between the two polypeptide chains.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from mass photometry data.

claim: The higher degree of HDX protection detected in the active site and key regulatory regions of the enzyme suggests that the structural organization that occurs in the phosphorylated enzyme, [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P, is important for enzymatic activity.
source: The higher degree of HDX protection detected in the active site and key regulatory regions of the enzyme (Figure 1C and D) suggests that the structural organization that occurs in the phosphorylated enzyme, [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P, is important for enzymatic activity.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from HDX-MS data shown in Figure 1C and D.

claim: The results are consistent with similar studies on other protein kinases where phosphorylation of the threonine residue in the activation loop leads to rigidification of the structure.
source: Our results are consistent with similar studies on other protein kinases where phosphorylation of the threonine residue in the activation loop leads to rigidification of the structure (Lorenzen and Pawson, 2014; Steichen et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: A 2.8 μs MD simulation of the enzyme complex was performed in the phosphorylated, [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P, and the unphosphorylated, [Aurora B/IN-box]no-P states using the available X-ray structure (PDB 4C2W) as a template.
source: To gain insight into the structural rearrangements during the autoactivation process at atomic resolution, we performed a 2.8 μs MD simulation of the enzyme complex in the phosphorylated, [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P, and the unphosphorylated, [Aurora B/IN-box]no-P states using the available X-ray structure (PDB 4C2W) (Sessa and Villa, 2014) as a template (see Materials and methods and Figure 2).
evidence: The claim describes the MD simulation methodology.

claim: During the simulation, the systems were stable and retained the tertiary and quaternary structures in the folded regions of the complex.
source: During the simulation, the systems were stable and retained the tertiary and quaternary structures in the folded regions of the complex (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by MD simulation data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The major structural differences between the two forms of the enzyme complex were observed in the conformation of the C-terminal part of IN-box and in the conformation of the activation loop.
source: The major structural differences between the two forms of the enzyme complex were observed in the conformation of the C-terminal part of IN-box and in the conformation of the activation loop.
evidence: The claim is supported by MD simulation data.

claim: In the MD simulation of [Aurora B/IN-box]no-P, the C-terminal part of IN-box remains unstructured and does not stably interact with Aurora B throughout the simulation period.
source: In the MD simulation of [Aurora B/IN-box]no-P, where neither Aurora BThr248 nor the TSS motif of IN-box are phosphorylated, the IN-box showed great flexibility. Its C-terminal part remains unstructured and does not stably interact with Aurora B throughout the simulation period (Figure 2A and Video 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by MD simulation data shown in Figure 2A and Video 1.

claim: The simulations of phosphorylated [Aurora B/IN-box] showed that the presence of phosphates in Aurora B and IN-box rapidly stabilizes a defined conformation in which the C-terminal region of IN-box interacts with the Aurora B activation loop.
source: On the contrary, the simulations of phosphorylated [Aurora B/IN-box] showed that the presence of phosphates in Aurora B and IN-box rapidly stabilizes a defined conformation in which the C-terminal region of IN-box interacts with the Aurora B activation loop (Figure 2A and Video 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by MD simulation data shown in Figure 2A and Video 2.

claim: IN-boxArg847 forms an electrostatic interaction with the phospho-threonine of the activation loop, Aurora BpThr248, early in the simulation (0.7 μs), and this interaction remains stable until the end of the simulation.
source: Moreover, IN-boxArg847 forms an electrostatic interaction with the phospho-threonine of the activation loop, Aurora BpThr248, early in the simulation (0.7 μs), and this interaction remains stable until the end of the simulation (the next 1.8 μs) (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by MD simulation data shown in Figure 2B and C.

claim: Aurora BpThr248 is stabilized by four arginine residues: IN-boxArg847, Aurora BArg246, Aurora BArg247, and Aurora BArg215 from the catalytic loop (HRD).
source: In addition to IN-boxArg847, Aurora BpThr248 is stabilized by three arginine residues from Aurora B - two adjacent residues in the activation loop, Aurora BArg246 and Aurora BArg247, and Aurora BArg215 from the catalytic loop (HRD), closely resembling equivalent interactions in the Aurora C observed in [Aurora C/IN-box] crystal structure. Thus, stabilization of negative phosphate in the [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P activation loop involves interaction with four arginine residues
evidence: The claim is supported by MD simulation data.

claim: Stabilization of negative phosphate in the [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P activation loop is more extensive than phosphate stabilization in the initial structure (PDB 4C2W), in which Aurora BpThr248 is present but the IN-box TSS motif is absent.
source: and is more extensive than phosphate stabilization in the initial structure (PDB 4C2W), in which Aurora BpThr248 is present but the IN-box TSS motif is absent (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of MD simulation data with the initial crystal structure shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: An important common feature between the [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P simulation and the [Aurora C/IN-box]all-P crystal structure is that the IN-box interacts with the kinase activation loop stabilizing the active state of the kinase by reducing dynamics and favoring a more compact enzyme.
source: An important common feature between our [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P simulation and the [Aurora C/IN-box]all-P crystal structure is that the IN-box interacts with the kinase activation loop stabilizing the active state of the kinase by reducing dynamics and favoring a more compact enzyme.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of MD simulation data with the crystal structure.

claim: The structure from the [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P simulation and the [Aurora C/IN-box]all-P crystal structure are very similar overall.
source: Overall, the structure from our [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P simulation and the [Aurora C/IN-box]all-P crystal structure are very similar.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of MD simulation data with the crystal structure.

claim: An important difference exists in the C-terminal IN-box region between the [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P simulation and the [Aurora C/IN-box]all-P crystal structure.
source: However, an important difference exists in the C-terminal IN-box region (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of MD simulation data with the crystal structure shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: In the [Aurora B/IN box]all-P simulation, the C-terminal region of the IN-box is extended further toward the C-terminal lobe of the kinase and interacts with the phosphorylated activation segment.
source: In the [Aurora B/IN box]all-P simulation, the C-terminal region of the IN-box is extended further toward the C-terminal lobe of the kinase and interacts with the phosphorylated activation segment
evidence: The claim is supported by MD simulation data.

claim: In the [Aurora C/IN-box]all-P crystal structure there are reciprocal interaction in which arginines from the activation loop interact with the phosphorylated TSS motif of the IN-box.
source: whereas in the [Aurora C/IN-box]all-P crystal structure there are reciprocal interaction in which arginines from the activation loop interact with the phosphorylated TSS motif of the IN-box.
evidence: The claim is based on the crystal structure of [Aurora C/IN-box]all-P.

claim: The crystal structure of [Aurora C/IN-box]all-P is more likely to represent the final active conformational state of the enzyme complex.
source: We suggest that the crystal structure of [Aurora C/IN-box]all-P is more likely to represent the final active conformational state of the enzyme complex
evidence: The claim is based on speculation and inference from MD simulation data.

claim: The [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P from the simulation is more likely an intermediate state on the autoactivation trajectory.
source: and that the [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P from our simulation is more likely an intermediate state on the autoactivation trajectory.
evidence: The claim is based on speculation and inference from MD simulation data.

claim: The C-terminal part of the IN-box is anchored to Aurora B only by side-chain interactions, whereas the main-chain hydrogens do not form stable hydrogen networks, leaving this region free for HDX despite a different conformation.
source: First, the C-terminal part of the IN-box is anchored to Aurora B only by side-chain interactions, whereas the main-chain hydrogens do not form stable hydrogen networks, leaving this region free for HDX despite a different conformation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from MD simulation data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The RMSFs for the N-terminal part of the IN-box, IN-box807-837, are significantly higher in [Aurora B/IN-box]no-P than in [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P.
source: We calculated the root mean square fluctuations (RMSFs) during MS simulations for the N-terminal part of the IN-box, IN-box807-837, in the two forms of the enzyme complex (black coil in Figure 2D). Higher RMSF are associated with larger structural deformations. Consistent with the HDX results, the RMSFs for this region are significantly higher in [Aurora B/IN-box]no-P than in [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P (Figure 2D, graph).
evidence: The claim is supported by MD simulation data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: In the dephosphorylated state, Aurora BαC exhibits a very broad RMSF distribution shifted toward higher values, consistent with strong helix deformations.
source: In the dephosphorylated state, Aurora BαC exhibits a very broad RMSF distribution shifted toward higher values, consistent with strong helix deformations.
evidence: The claim is supported by MD simulation data.

claim: The RMSF values in [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P show a narrow distribution, clearly indicating a more structured Aurora BαC.
source: In contrast, the RMSF values in [Aurora B/IN-box]all-P show a narrow distribution, clearly indicating a more structured Aurora BαC.
evidence: The claim is supported by MD simulation data.

claim: The Aurora B regions in contact with the N-terminal IN-box segment are structurally more disordered in the absence of phosphorylation than when the enzyme complex is fully phosphorylated.
source: In summary, the Aurora B regions in contact with the N-terminal IN-box segment are structurally more disordered in the absence of phosphorylation than when the enzyme complex is fully phosphorylated, strongly suggesting that the dynamics of the adjacent regions of Aurora B and IN-box are coupled.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from MD simulation data.

claim: In the unphosphorylated form of the enzyme complex the structural disorder spreads from one partner to the other.
source: In the unphosphorylated form of the enzyme complex the structural disorder spreads from one partner to the other.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from MD simulation data.

claim: The IN-box could act as a negative regulator of the kinase activity by transferring disorder to the kinase domain.
source: Therefore, the IN-box could act as a negative regulator of the kinase activity by transferring disorder to the kinase domain.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from MD simulation and HDX data.

claim: Structural order is imposed on both Aurora B and the IN-box by phosphorylation.
source: Conversely, structural order is imposed on both Aurora B and the IN-box by phosphorylation.
